# Ownership and bounds
The L1 (KotodamaR56) is the sole integration owner and holds the canonical planner seat. Every seat is a leaf: no delegation, no background jobs, no swarms (an executor may spawn at most one read-only labrat probe). Every `Report:` trailer path is relative to /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/kotodama-shokunin — write it at /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/kotodama-shokunin/<that path>; never write under /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/.ufo or anywhere else in the fleet repo. Seats write ONLY their own report file (executors may also write under their scratch dir). NEVER edit, create or delete any other file in /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/kotodama-shokunin, a sibling lane, or the fleet repo /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin. Never run git or jj writes in the lane or the fleet repo: no commit, push, add, stash, checkout, reset, ref update, index or jj state change; read-only git (log, show, diff, status, archive) is fine; in the lane only read-only jj with --ignore-working-copy, and never any jj at the fleet root. Scratch goes under /fast/scratch/hyaku/kotodama-r56/<SeatName>/. The only message target is agent://KotodamaR56; never message agent://all. Finish with your report written; a seat that cannot finish still writes what it has and says what is missing.

# Sources
External web reading is allowed by ORDINARY MEANS ONLY: plain requests (read tool, curl), public copies, archive.org or Wayback captures, open repositories. NEVER use a headless browser or any tool to get past a bot challenge, captcha, paywall, login or other access control (QUALITY criterion 10); archive.org controlled-lending (borrow) books need a login and do not count. A challenge met and then routed around by an ordinary copy (a Wayback capture) must be reported as "challenge met, not passed". A source counts only if you opened it in this session. For each opened source give: the URL you actually read (the file you quote from, not only its landing page), the route (direct with HTTP status, or the Wayback capture id), access date 2026-10-22, and 2-4 verbatim quotes of AT MOST 25 WORDS EACH, each with its exact locator (page, section or paragraph). Never join two fragments into one quote; give them as separate quotes. Never repeat the locator as a quoted string. Write quotes and every other field as plain UTF-8 text: never HTML entities such as " or “ (round 55 leaked 16 of them into its Gate). Prefer primary sources: early-modern texts in public-domain scans (archive.org, Gallica, Biodiversity Heritage Library, HathiTrust full-view), museum collection records written by the holding museum, official heritage bodies (UNESCO), open-access peer-reviewed papers (Persée, Cambridge Core open access, university repositories), community statements. Tier per /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/kotodama-shokunin/corpus/QUALITY.md criterion 6: an abstract or publisher description is tier B; tier A only for a source primary or authoritative for the exact scope. Wikipedia and similar are tier C leads only. Pirate or shadow-library copies are not ordinary public copies: never use them.

# Tooling
You and every seat may install or upgrade tools that help the task; read /home/vgpnk/.omp/agent/RULES.md first and record tool, version, channel and reason. All pacman transactions are PAUSED host-wide: never pacman -S/-Sy/-Syu/-U/-R, never downgrade, never restart a host service; use uv tool, npx or an official binary in ~/.local/bin, or report the need. Prefer no installs.

# Output
A concise Markdown report at your Report path. Source seats use exactly this shape per source: `### NEW-<SeatName>-<n>` then lines `citation:` (author, year, title, venue, stable id), `url:`, `route:`, `kind:` (paper, book, dataset, web, record, community), `tier:` (A/B/C with a one-line reason), `scope:` (what the row may support), `quotes:` (bulleted, each `<locator>: "<quote>"`), `teaches:` (ONE complete sentence of at most 30 words, ending with a full stop), then `draft sentences:` — 3 to 6 sentences for the entry, each ending with `(NEW-<SeatName>-<n>, <locator>)`, each saying only what a quote or the opened page carries, at the strength the page states (keep hedges such as 'probably', 'by tradition', 'according to'), aimed at what a worldbuilder must decide. End with `unopened:` (sources tried and not opened, with the reason). Other seats: findings with file:line or URL evidence, result, unrun checks. Write plain English: no run-together words, no private jargon. Name communities, polities and places precisely (Kongo kingdom, Kikongo/Koongo language, Mbanza Kongo/São Salvador, Soyo, Mbata); no exoticizing language ('fetish' only inside a quotation and flagged as the source's word).
